ATTRIBUTION_GAP: OutgoingEntranceCone.heightThreshold (OutgoingEntranceCone.lean:1812) is min(1/100, lam/4, exp(-(entranceTime m + 3/5))/8), with entranceTime m = e^m+12 = T_d+2 (line 1226). amplitudeThreshold m = exp(e^m+11)+1 > e^{T_d}. Both are used in the ordered chain at :2156.

Definition 3.3 (p.18) is a reading convention: ≪ means sufficiently small given the data already fixed, choices go right to left, large parameters come from small reciprocals, and smallness is uniform over profile domains. Page 19 holds only Table 1. Nothing in NavierStokes/ defines ≪ or cites Definition 3.3, so the relation is absent. Lean encodes each use through binder order, which is why the ledger is CONVENTION. All three voters agree. I verified every cited declaration in decls.jsonl and the source. Following the PAIRING skeptic, I added exists_ordered_actual_preliminary_cone, heightThreshold and exists_scheduled_family_below as the closest instances of the (A.6) chain (p.129). They show the e^{-T_d} cap is present, contrary to the auditor's consequence text. The auditor's page and count citations were corrected.

findings.summary: A repository search found no Lean declaration that defines ≪ or states Definition 3.3's order-of-choices convention in general. The uses examined are encoded as quantifier order or explicit caps. Not all 26 occurrences of ≪ in the paper were traced.

The auditor's consequence says Lean has only 2h<λ where (A.6) asks h ≪ min{λ, e^{-T_d}}. That holds for some statements only (OutgoingTail.TailData and several theorems constrain h by 2h<λ alone). heightThreshold carries the e^{-T_d} cap, and the full (A.6) order appears in exists_ordered_actual_preliminary_cone.
